did_you_know.text: Did you know? This prophecy was given to Baruch son of Neriah in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Did you know? Baruch was the one who wrote down Jeremiah the prophet’s words in a book—that is, on a scroll.
Did you know? The LORD addresses Baruch personally and delivers a message to him through Jeremiah.
Did you know? Baruch describes his distress with the words, “Woe is me!” He says that grief, pain, and groaning have overwhelmed him, and he has found no rest.
Did you know? The prophecy uses the imagery of building and planting: what the LORD has built, he is tearing down, and what he has planted, he is uprooting.
Did you know? The wording “and the whole land itself” emphasizes that the calamity described is not limited to one person but affects the entire land.
Did you know? Baruch is commanded not to seek “great things” for himself—extraordinary achievements or status—while the LORD is bringing disaster on all flesh.
Did you know? The promise given to Baruch is the preservation of his life: wherever he goes, his life will be given to him as a prize.
